finding.claim: Unauthenticated GET /rss passes the raw u query parameter to URI.open, which fetches any http/https URL with no host, IP, scheme, or redirect restrictions. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata.
finding.source: params[:u] in the get "/rss" route (app.rb:7-8). No auth guard on the route.
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read (app.rb:8), i.e. open-uri with an attacker-chosen URL, following redirects by default.

trace.note: Route get "/rss" has no authentication or authorization check.
params[:u] flows unchanged into URI.open; no parse, scheme allowlist, host/IP check, or redirect control.
open-uri fetches the URL and follows 3xx redirects, so an allowed external URL can redirect to http://169.254.169.254/ or RFC1918/loopback addresses.
data[0,400] returns the first 400 bytes of the fetched body to the attacker, making the SSRF readable rather than blind.

finding.guards_checked: No validation exists on this path. Checked: route auth (none in app.rb), parameter parsing (none), scheme allowlist (none), host or IP denylist (none), DNS pinning (none), redirect handling (open-uri default, follows redirects), and whether framework middleware could sanitize upstream (none is visible in this single-file app).

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:7 has no auth or validation on the "/rss" route, and app.rb:8 passes params[:u] straight to URI.open with no scheme, host, or IP check. The only guard in the file is the TRUSTED host check at app.rb:13-14, which belongs to the separate "/trusted" route and does not apply here.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated route at app.rb:7 passes params[:u] unchanged into URI.open at app.rb:8, open-uri follows http/https redirects by default, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes of the body, so the SSRF is readable and no closing guard exists on this path.

finding.claim: Adjacent to SSRF on the same sink: a non-URL value in u is handed to Kernel#open, which reads local files and, on Ruby versions that still support it, runs a command when the value begins with '|'. This is not SSRF, but it is the same unvalidated input and is likely more severe; verify the Ruby version before relying on the command path.
finding.sink: URI.open falls back to Kernel#open for strings that do not match a scheme (open-uri behavior), reaching File.open or the pipe form of Kernel#open.

trace.note: URI.open(params[:u]) receives a string without a scheme such as /etc/passwd or |id.
The first 400 bytes of the local file or command output are returned to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. Not verified by running the app; Ruby version and open-uri internals should be confirmed in the target environment.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:8 passes params[:u] straight to URI.open with no validation, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. The TRUSTED host check at app.rb:5 and app.rb:14 applies only to the /trusted route, not /rss.
verdict.reason: At app.rb:8, the unauthenticated query parameter params[:u] reaches URI.open with no check, so a scheme-less value such as /etc/passwd is read as a local file and its first 400 bytes are returned at app.rb:9. The command path (a leading '|') depends on the Ruby version and open-uri internals, which I could not check here since the repo has no Gemfile or .ruby-version, so the file read is the part I'd rely on.
